aia-vecchia-sor-ugo-bolgheri-superiore.producerStory: The Pellegrini family grew grapes in Bolgheri for generations, selling fruit to the area's famous estates before founding Aia Vecchia in 1995, named after an old farm building on their land. Sor Ugo is their flagship — a Bordeaux-style blend first developed with noted enologist Tibor Gál and launched in 2001, named for Ugo, the first Pellegrini to work with vines a century ago ('Sor' is an old honorific for Signor).
aia-vecchia-sor-ugo-bolgheri-superiore.whyWePourIt: Our Super Tuscan slot: coastal Bolgheri's ripe, cedar-and-dark-fruit power for the steak-and-statement-red guest, without trophy-label pricing.

algre-valganon.producerStory: Husband-and-wife team Óscar Alegre and Eva Valgañón, who met studying enology in Italy, have made wine since 2014 in Fonzaleche — a village of about 80 people that is one of the highest, coldest corners of far-western Rioja Alta. They farm small old parcels in Fonzaleche and nearby Sajazarra, often ferment with stems, and use only neutral French oak — deliberately the opposite of big, oaky commercial Rioja.
algre-valganon.whyWePourIt: The Rioja that surprises people who think they know Rioja — floral, fresh and gentle, our high-altitude answer to a Burgundy-drinker's red.

alta-mora-etna-rosso.producerStory: Alta Mora — 'high and black,' for Etna's altitude and dark volcanic soils — is the Sicilian Cusumano brothers' Mount Etna project, begun in 2013 when they bought their first vineyard contrade on the volcano's north slope and rebuilt the traditional dry-stone terraces. The grapes are estate-grown, hand-harvested Nerello Mascalese from some of Europe's highest vineyards, including very old vines in Contrada Guardiola.
alta-mora-etna-rosso.whyWePourIt: Our volcanic light red — the 'Sicilian Pinot Noir' for the elegant-red drinker who wants something savoury, mineral and a little exotic.

bideona-cabezadas.producerStory: Bideona is a village-and-vineyard-focused winery in Villabuena de Álava, Rioja Alavesa, backed by Basque txakoli producer Gorka Izagirre and run by the Península Vinicultores team. It farms over 300 tiny old parcels — average age around 50 years — across the villages of Rioja Alavesa. 'Cabezadas' are the high tops of those vineyards where white vines were traditionally planted, and this is an unoaked, mostly-Viura field blend from them.
bideona-cabezadas.whyWePourIt: A crisp, stony old-vine white at our friendliest bottle price — the insider's alternative when a guest asks for 'just a dry white'.

brandini-langhe-filari-corti.producerStory: Agricola Brandini is a roughly 25-hectare estate in the high-altitude zones of La Morra, in Barolo country, run by young sisters Serena and Giovanna Bagnasco and certified organic since 2011. Filari Corti is their Langhe Nebbiolo: picked earlier than their Barolo fruit and aged in large oak, so it leads with bright red fruit, roses and silky La Morra tannins.
brandini-langhe-filari-corti.whyWePourIt: The gateway Nebbiolo — Barolo-country perfume and structure at a third of Barolo money, perfect with charcuterie or anything truffled.

castello-di-potentino-sacromonte.producerStory: Castello di Potentino is an ancient castle estate on the slopes of Monte Amiata, Tuscany's extinct volcano, restored and run by English winemaker Charlotte Horton, who has made wine in Tuscany for over two decades. She ferments with native yeasts and minimal intervention; Sacromonte, her 100% Sangiovese, is named for the 'sacred mountain' the Etruscans believed was home of the gods.
castello-di-potentino-sacromonte.whyWePourIt: Sangiovese with a story — a castle, a volcano and an Englishwoman — pouring fresher and more mineral than Chianti for the curious red drinker.

castello-di-verduno-alba.producerStory: Castello di Verduno is run from a 16th-century castle in Verduno, in Barolo country, owned by the Burlotto family since 1909 — the same family behind the famed G.B. Burlotto estate next door. Today Gabriella Burlotto and Franco Bianco run it with their daughters and longtime winemaker Mario Andrion, farming about 10 hectares split between Verduno and Barbaresco; the Barbera comes from a tiny old parcel planted in the 1950s and '60s.
castello-di-verduno-alba.whyWePourIt: Juicy, high-acid, low-tannin Piedmont red from a storied Barolo-family castle — our most food-flexible Italian pour.

charlotte-jean-baptiste-senat-amalgame.producerStory: Charlotte and Jean-Baptiste Sénat left Paris in 1995 for Jean-Baptiste's family land in Trausse, in the Minervois hills of the Languedoc, and became pioneers of natural winemaking there — organic farming, native varieties, no fining or filtration. Amalgame is their pale, gluggable cuvée: old southern varieties (Grenache noir and gris with Piquepoul, Counoise and Terret) co-fermented whole-cluster and bottled young.
charlotte-jean-baptiste-senat-amalgame.whyWePourIt: Our chillable natural red — barely-there tannin and garrigue-scented red fruit for patio season and the orange-wine crowd.

christophe-mignon-adn-de-meunier-brut-na.producerStory: Christophe Mignon is a fifth-generation grower in Festigny and Le Breuil in the Vallée de la Marne, farming about 6.5 hectares that are roughly 90% Pinot Meunier — vines his great-grandparents planted. He farms by biodynamic principles and the lunar calendar, and ADN de Meunier is his calling card: 100% Meunier, long lees aging, and zero dosage, so it finishes bone-dry.
christophe-mignon-adn-de-meunier-brut-na.whyWePourIt: Our grower-Champagne statement — proof that humble Meunier, in obsessive hands, can be laser-focused and savoury rather than simply fruity.

chateau-larose-perganson.producerStory: Larose Perganson's origins trace to 1719, when Jean-Pierre de Pontet founded the estate in the Haut-Médoc; today it is part of Vignobles de Larose and made in the cellars of its larger neighbour, Château Larose-Trintaudon, near Saint-Laurent-du-Médoc. It carries Cru Bourgeois Supérieur status and is a classic Cabernet-Merlot left-bank claret in the cedar-and-blackcurrant mould.
chateau-larose-perganson.whyWePourIt: The classic Bordeaux slot — savoury, structured left-bank claret with real age-worthiness for the traditionalist at the table.

cirelli-frizzante-bianco.producerStory: Francesco Cirelli founded his 22-hectare certified-organic farm near Atri, in Abruzzo's Teramo hills a few kilometres from the Adriatic, in 2003 — a true mixed farm with olives, figs, wheat, geese and pigs alongside the vines, best known for fermenting in terracotta amphorae. The Frizzante Bianco is his easy-going side: Trebbiano with a gentle natural sparkle, spontaneously fermented and low in alcohol.
cirelli-frizzante-bianco.whyWePourIt: Our relaxed aperitif fizz — softer and friendlier than Champagne, low-alcohol, and a natural fit for sessions that start before dinner.

ciro-picariello-bru-emm.producerStory: Ciro Picariello is one of Campania's most respected white-wine growers, famous above all for Fiano di Avellino from high-altitude vineyards around Summonte and Montefredane; he and his wife founded the estate in 1997. BruEmm — named for the youngest family generation, Bruno and Emma — is his Falanghina, from a vineyard he farms near Benevento at around 400 metres, aged briefly in stainless steel to keep it fresh.
ciro-picariello-bru-emm.whyWePourIt: A southern-Italian crisp white with a saline snap — the off-the-beaten-path alternative to Pinot Grigio from a cult Fiano producer.

claire-naudin-mallon.producerStory: Claire Naudin runs her family's Domaine Henri Naudin-Ferrand in Magny-lès-Villers, in the Hautes-Côtes above Burgundy's Côte d'Or, which she took over from her father in 1994. She is one of Burgundy's most outspoken champions of the underdog Aligoté grape, working with minimal intervention and very low sulfur; Mallon is her textured, lees-aged Bourgogne Aligoté.
claire-naudin-mallon.whyWePourIt: Insider Burgundy — the sommelier's grape from a cult low-intervention grower, scratching the white-Burgundy itch without white-Burgundy pricing.

clos-bellane-valreas.producerStory: Clos Bellane is a single high-altitude estate in the hills above Valréas, at the cool northern edge of the southern Rhône, bought in 2010 by winemaker Stéphane Vedeau with the goal of making fresher styles of Côtes du Rhône Villages. The vineyards sit at roughly 400 metres on limestone and were converted to certified organic farming; whites come from Marsanne, Roussanne and Viognier.
clos-bellane-valreas.whyWePourIt: Our richer-but-still-fresh Rhône white — peachy and floral with a stony finish, the step between crisp whites and full Chardonnay.

cusumano-lucido.producerStory: Cusumano was founded in 2001 by brothers Diego and Alberto Cusumano in Partinico, west of Palermo, and has grown into one of Sicily's leading estates with vineyards across the island. Lucido is the local name for the finer clone of Catarratto, western Sicily's historic white grape — this bottling keeps it bright, unoaked and sunny.
cusumano-lucido.whyWePourIt: The easy Sicilian opener — ripe, friendly and our most accessible white, an honest by-the-bottle value for groups.

denizot-sancerre.producerStory: Domaine Denizot is an eight-generation family estate in Verdigny, in the heart of Sancerre, today led by Thibauld Denizot with his parents Chantal and Christian. They farm about 19 hectares — three-quarters Sauvignon Blanc — mostly on the prized limestone 'caillottes' soils around Amigny and Chavignol, with minimal intervention in the cellar.
denizot-sancerre.whyWePourIt: The benchmark crisp white — flinty, bone-dry Sancerre that needs no explanation and flatters oysters, martinis and people-watching alike.

domaine-breton-pierres-rousses.producerStory: Catherine and Pierre Breton are pioneers of the Loire's natural-wine movement, farming organically/biodynamically in Bourgueil since the 1980s, with family vines in Catherine's native Vouvray. Pierres Rousses comes from roughly 55-year-old Chenin Blanc on flinty clay ('pierres rousses') soils, fermented and aged in used barrels to a dry, textured style — a cuvée associated with the next generation, their son Paul, who focuses on the whites.
domaine-breton-pierres-rousses.whyWePourIt: Grown-up dry Chenin — waxy texture and quince over Loire acidity, our pick for guests who want a white with grip and a natural-wine pedigree.

domaine-buisson-charles-meursault-vieill.producerStory: Domaine Buisson-Charles is a small family estate in Meursault dating back over a century, now run by Patrick Essa — son-in-law of third-generation vigneron Michel Buisson — with his wife Catherine. From about 6 hectares, Essa has pushed the domaine into Meursault's top rank; the Vieilles Vignes comes from old parcels (vines of roughly 60 to 100 years) and is raised in barrel with restrained new oak for a rich-but-chiselled style.
domaine-buisson-charles-meursault-vieill.whyWePourIt: The celebration white — true old-vine Meursault with hazelnut and cream over a mineral spine, for the table that wants the best Chardonnay in the house.

domaine-gour-de-chaule-gigondas-les-jard.producerStory: Domaine du Gour de Chaulé was founded in 1900 by Eugène Bonfils in the heart of Gigondas village and has been passed down largely through the family's women — today fourth-generation Stéphanie Fumoso runs it, joined by her son Paul in 2018. Its 10 hectares of old vines across many small parcels are raised traditionally in concrete tanks and old foudres; Les Jardinières is a Grenache-led blend with Syrah and Mourvèdre.
domaine-gour-de-chaule-gigondas-les-jard.whyWePourIt: Our plush southern-Rhône GSM — old-vine Gigondas warmth, garrigue and supple tannin for the guest who wants generosity without jamminess.

domaine-de-colette-coteaux-de-colette.producerStory: Domaine de Colette is a 16-hectare family estate in Lantignié, on the edge of Beaujolais' Régnié and Morgon crus, officially created in 1953 by René Gauthier and run today by his son Jacky with his wife Evelyne. The Gamay vines grow on pink granite with an average age around 55 years (some over 80), hand-harvested and farmed organically (in conversion since 2020).
domaine-de-colette-coteaux-de-colette.whyWePourIt: The breeziest red on the list — old-vine cru-country Gamay that takes a light chill and bridges rosé drinkers into red territory.

domaine-de-la-rochette-macon-bussieres-m.producerStory: Domaine de la Rochette farms about 10 hectares in Bussières and Milly-Lamartine in the Mâconnais, and since 2015 has been part-owned and made by Frédéric-Marc Burrier of Maison Joseph Burrier — the family behind Château de Beauregard in Pouilly-Fuissé. The Mont Sard cuvée comes from a parcel of vines on the steep, stony marly-limestone slopes beneath Mont Sard itself, giving unusually concentrated Mâcon Chardonnay.
domaine-de-la-rochette-macon-bussieres-m.whyWePourIt: White Burgundy flavour at Mâcon money — creamy, nutty old-vine Chardonnay that overdelivers for its place on the list.

donnhoff-feinherb.producerStory: The Dönnhoff family has farmed in Oberhausen on the Nahe river for over 250 years, and under Helmut Dönnhoff — and now his son Cornelius, winemaker since 2007 — the estate became one of Germany's most acclaimed Riesling producers, a member of the VDP with about 25 hectares of top sites. Wines are pressed quickly after picking and fermented in traditional casks and steel for purity.
donnhoff-feinherb.whyWePourIt: Our barely-off-dry Riesling from a legendary grower — the trace of sweetness makes it the list's best friend for spice, heat and salt.

eleonore-moreau-petit-chablis.producerStory: Eléonore Moreau farms her family's 13 hectares in Poilly-sur-Serein, at the southeastern edge of the Chablis appellation, under the label Domaine des Pérégrins — vines her father planted in the early 1980s on land the family has held for generations. She returned in 2011, took over winemaking in 2016, pushed through organic certification, and ages her Petit Chablis unusually long on the lees in tank for extra texture.
eleonore-moreau-petit-chablis.whyWePourIt: Oyster-shell Chablis character from a small organic grower — steely, flinty and a sharp-value alternative to bigger-name Chablis.

fletcher-barbaresco-recta-pete.producerStory: Dave Fletcher is an Adelaide-trained Australian who moved to Piedmont in 2007 to work for the famed Ceretto estate, rising to a senior winemaking role there before building his own label inside Barbaresco's converted old train station. Recta Pete — 'shoot straight' in his family's Scots dialect — is his classic-style Barbaresco, blending fruit from top crus, fermented with native yeasts and aged about two years in old oak, bottled unfiltered.
fletcher-barbaresco-recta-pete.whyWePourIt: Barbaresco's perfume and polish with a great story — the outsider-made-good bottle for the guest choosing between elegance and power.

griesel-blanc-de-noirs.producerStory: Griesel & Compagnie, founded in 2013 in Bensheim, was the first dedicated sparkling-wine house on the Hessische Bergstraße, one of Germany's smallest wine regions, working from a historic 1904 vaulted cellar. Cellar master Niko Brandner — who trained with Volker Raumland, Germany's leading sparkling specialist — makes everything by traditional bottle fermentation; the Blanc de Noirs is Pinot Noir and Meunier with at least 20 months on the lees.
griesel-blanc-de-noirs.whyWePourIt: Our German answer to Champagne — traditional-method Sekt with brioche depth and crisp drive, a conversation-starting pour at a fair price.
